item.title: Blocks: I Wish I Knew w/ Neal Brennan: Bobby Lee: I Wish I Knew
item.description:
Why: Bobby Lee with Neal Brennan on Blocks: your favorite pairing, and a candid talk on sobriety, his father's death, and career.
Originally released 2026-10-29. Score 96.
Bobby Lee joins Neal Brennan to share what he wishes he knew sooner: worrying about his career wouldn’t change its course, asking for help mattered, and the life he built could look different from the one he imagined. He still likes the MadTV tattoo, though. They talk about Bobby’s first stand-up special, learning to watch himself on screen, sobriety, his father’s death, and the unexpected emotional impact of a trip to Build-A-Bear. Plus: homemade glue hands, a swimming pool full of coffee, Neal’s place in the comedy police, and whether he’s allowed to speak at Bobby’s funeral. ---------------

item.title: Making Sense with Sam Harris: #499 — The Birth of AGI
item.description:
Why: Sam Harris with Kevin Roose on the AGI race, Amodei and AI risk; short.
Originally released 2026-10-20. Score 93.
Sam Harris speaks with Kevin Roose about the race to build artificial general intelligence. They discuss Roose's book The AGI Chronicles, the scaling laws behind AI's rapid progress, Dario Amodei's "big blob of compute" memo, the birth of reasoning models, Roose's encounter with Bing's Sydney chatbot, the roughly 50 people deciding humanity's future, the rivalries among lab leaders, AI agents and recursive self-improvement, the absence of regulation, and other topics. item.title: The Diary Of A CEO with Steven Bartlett: Dr. Sarah Paine: Why The World Is Turning Away From America
item.description:
Why: Sarah Paine on great power strategy and maritime order, an automatic yes and a past star.
Originally released 2026-10-29. Score 97.
Are escalating geopolitical tensions hurtling humanity towards World War III? Dr. Sarah Paine highlights the historical roots of geopolitical conflicts and demonstrates how shifting away from a rules-based maritime order guarantees economic collapse. Dr. Sarah Paine is a renowned geopolitical strategist, historian, and retired professor from the U.S. Naval War College, specializing in Russian and Chinese imperial history and maritime strategy.
